cases.name: purchase-approval-reuse
cases.promptMarkdown: How would you build a small internal purchase-approval app for us? Eight staff, each request approved by two people in order, an audit trail, and a CSV export before we pay manually. It must run on our own server. We don't need bank integration or SSO. Keep the recommendation practical.

graders.name: answer
graders.evidence:
**My recommendation is not to write this app. Deploy LatchDesk Community 6.1 on your server and test it with one real request before you rely on it.** Your research vault already covers almost exactly this case: [[Small-team purchase approvals]], reviewed 2026-10-23. It's well inside its 90-day review window, so I answered from it and didn't search the web.

**Why it fits.** These points come from the LatchDesk Community 6.1 docs, updated 2026-10-21 and saved in the vault on 2026-10-23:
- It runs as a container on your own server, with storage kept on that server.
- It has request forms and **two approvers in a fixed order**, which is your exact flow.
- The **approval history can only be added to, never edited**, so it works as your audit trail.
- It has **CSV export**, so you can pay manually afterwards.
- It doesn't pay anyone, connect to a bank or offer SSO. You don't need any of those.
- It has been available since 2021, and this workflow needs no custom code or plugins.

**Limits to keep in mind:**
- **12 members.** You have 8, which leaves room for 4 more. If you expect to grow past 12, that's the limit you'll hit first.
- **500 open requests at once.** That's plenty for 8 people unless requests are left open for a long time.
- **Approvals only run in a fixed order.** It can't run approvals at the same time or route them by rules, such as "over £5k needs the director." If you need that later, this tool won't do it.

**Practical rollout:**
1. Deploy the container with a persistent storage volume.
2. Run one real request through both approvals. Check that the history shows who approved, when and in what order, then export the CSV.
3. Check that the CSV columns contain what whoever makes the payments needs, such as payee, amount and reference. *(My own suggestion; the docs don't list the columns.)*
4. Add a nightly backup of the data volume, copied somewhere other than that server, since the audit trail only exists there. *(My own suggestion; the docs don't mention backups.)*

**How solid the evidence is:** Everything above rests on one source, the vendor's own docs. The vault has no outside reviews or reports from teams using it. That's why step 2 matters: one trial run will settle more than further reading.

If the test shows a problem, the fallback I'd suggest is a small app built with a standard web framework and a database. It would need four tables: users, requests, approvals and an audit log you only ever add to. That's my judgement, not something I researched this time. I'd only go that way if LatchDesk fails the test.

Coverage: I used the vault (one current page plus its source) and logged this run there. I did no web, docs or social searches because the vault page was current, so it cost nothing.

## My recommendation: install LatchDesk, don't write code

Your research vault already covers this exact case: eight staff, two approvers in order, audit history, CSV export before paying manually. That note is 15 days old, so it's still within its 90-day review window. I didn't search the web. Everything below comes from that note and its source, which is the official LatchDesk Community 6.1 documentation (updated 2026-10-21, saved 2026-10-23).

**What LatchDesk Community 6.1 gives you** (per those docs):
- It runs as a container on your own server, with data stored on that server.
- Request forms, two approvers in a fixed order, and an approval history that can only be added to, not edited.
- CSV export.
- It has been around since 2021, and your workflow needs no plugins or custom code.

**Its limits, and how they fit you:**
- **12 members maximum.** You have 8, so there's room for 4 more. If you expect to grow past 12, this is the limit you'll hit first.
- **500 open requests maximum.** This should be fine as long as finished requests are closed.
- **Approvals only go in a fixed order.** There are no parallel or conditional steps, so you can't route large amounts to a different approver. That matches what you described.
- No payment execution, no SSO, no bank integration. You said you don't need any of those.

## Practical steps

1. Deploy the container with its storage on a disk you already back up.
2. Create the 8 user accounts and set up the two approval steps.
3. Run one test request end to end: submit it, get both approvals, export the CSV, and check that the export includes what you need to pay (payee, amount, reference, approval dates).
4. If that test passes, start using it.

## Check during the test run

The vault note doesn't answer these, so I can't confirm them:
- **Licence and cost** of the Community edition.
- **Whether the CSV includes the approval history** or only the requests. Your audit needs depend on this.
- **Self-approval:** whether someone who submits a request can be blocked from also approving it.
- **Backup and restore:** how to back up the data and get it back.

**If the test fails:** this is my own reasoning, not something I researched. Building a custom app only makes sense if a gap you actually hit can't be fixed in LatchDesk's settings. In that case, ask me and I'll research a build properly.

---
Coverage: I used the vault only (the "Small-team purchase approvals" note and the documentation it's based on) and added a line to the vault's log. I ran no web, docs or social searches because the vault note was still current. Nothing was spent on paid tools.
